observations: Target shark rises and changes viewing orientation while carrying a visible scrap; trunk/caudal silhouette changes during successive head directions.

limits: Camera motion, depth changes and occlusion prohibit calibrated3D yaw/phase measurements.

sources.reviewed: Actual full-duration24-frame overviews of Videos4,7,8; detailed Video7 17–21sec at6fps. Videos1,2,3,5,6 not visually reviewed this turn.
observations: Video7 near19–20sec: approach toward hand, mouth opens, closes and the whole animal passes/turns away; snout does not stay parked while jaws perform a long isolated loop.
Video4 and7 overviews show changes across the body and tail during turns; the sparse overviews do not establish a tail-to-head phase value.
limits: Human provisioning/handling can alter behavior; not a normal open-water hunting template.
Low resolution and crowding obscure jaw contacts; do not derive a precise gape angle or force from this.

sources.reviewed: 80.35sec launch trailer sampled every2sec;29–33sec inspected8fps. Actual external game frames, not merely a description of controls.
observations: Around30–31sec shark body and tail change shape/direction during a bite; target limbs move relative to grip, followed by release/consumption feedback.
Around31.1–32.8sec shark/orca combat uses full-body turning and target response, with very exaggerated effects.
limits: Quick edits, camera motion and possible slow-motion; cannot infer continuous attack timing from across cuts.
Good for readable attack/target/recovery staging, not a realistic amplitude or anatomy template.

findings.code: r4/capture_feeding.gd: controller.seek(1+t), then rigid carrier.rotation.y; r4/FeedingMotion.gd only head/jaw/floor overrides.
findings.conclusion: Native Swim keeps its own cycle while independent head shake is added; carrier yaw turns the entire rig rigidly. This does not create a feeding-specific curvature distribution down the trunk.
findings.next: Use one feeding action to blend head, anterior/mid trunk and caudal motion; choose bend distribution from a single continuous external shot. Keep head/body surface continuity.

findings.code: sin(PI*q)^2 * sin(TAU*3*q),1.85–2.85seconds; body fixed phase offset-.35rad.
findings.conclusion: Three perfectly prescribed oscillations were artistic guesses, not fitted to observed motion. Increasing8to14deg preserves this mechanical structure.
findings.next: Key a concrete grip/turn/reversal/recovery sequence against the reference; do not claim all real sharks are non-periodic or fit arbitrary irregular noise.

findings.code: prey pose from central jaw midpoint and feeding_head rotation; no independent flex/orientation response.
findings.conclusion: Prey behaves as a stiff crossbar attached to the mouth. Keeping the grip point fixed is useful, but the rest of the prey should not be forced to share the head transform exactly.
findings.next: Keep contact stable; animate free ends with lag/flex based on the selected prey and reference. Physics simulation is optional, not required.

findings.code: Gape.45/protrusion.85 remain constant after1.8sec; food carried to4.2sec.
findings.conclusion: Intentional grip-only prototype has no bite-off/regrip/release/swallow result; cannot stand in for a completed feeding event.
findings.next: Choose one evidenced ending for one prey size. Do not hide a prop to fake swallowing or apply ripping to every small fish.
